idea.why: Genuine three-role decomposition: two domain specialists that only classify, one composer that only presents, explicitly forbidden from inventing facts and confined to fragment markup. The deterministic page shell is kept out of the model entirely. Only soft spot is that the Merge is structurally load-bearing but semantically empty.

structure.why: Purpose-built types throughout, no Code node reimplementing something n8n already ships, and twelve nodes plus three explanatory stickies is proportionate. The one real quibble: all three agent nodes have no tools and no memory, so they are chains wearing an agent costume.

connections.why: Textbook. One trigger fans out to two genuinely independent fetches rather than serialising them, each lane chains only its real dependencies, and the streams rejoin exactly where they need to converge. Combine-by-position with unpaired items included, plus continue-on-error on both fetches, means one dead lane still produces a briefing rather than killing the run.

answer.why: End to end it does what was asked, and the CSS classes in the shell are precisely the ones the composer is instructed to emit, which is rare coherence and means the output renders as designed rather than as a blob. Two gaps: delivery is email only with nothing revisitable, and the fifty-message cap will silently truncate a busy inbox.

appraisal: The shape a competent author would reach for: fan out two independent fetches from one schedule, aggregate each lane so its agent fires once, run two narrow specialists off a single shared model, merge, then hand a composer the job of assembling fragments that a deterministic template wraps. The separation of judgement from presentation is the best thing here, and the prompts are defensive enough to survive a quiet day or a failed API call. What it gets wrong is small: two of the three agents are chains dressed as agents, and the Merge enforces join timing while the composer reads both reports by reference, making its data path decorative. First change: give the specialists a structured parser so the composer receives fields rather than prose, and raise the message cap.
